title: Noetherian flat geometrically integral algebra is projective
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring and let $R\to S$ be a finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] flat homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that every fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Then $S$ is a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and a field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and put $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the base change $(\operatorname{Spec}F)_K$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}K)$; it is integral by hypothesis, so by [def-pc-integral-scheme] it is nonempty and its ring $F\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}K$ is a nonzero integral domain. Tensor balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $F\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}K\cong S\otimes_RK$ by $(s\otimes a)\otimes t\mapsto s\otimes at$ and $s\otimes t\mapsto(s\otimes1)\otimes t$, so $S\otimes_RK$ is a nonzero integral domain. Suppose $S$ is not projective. Apply [lem-trf-projectivity-maximal-bad-reduced-quotient] to obtain $A=R/I$ and $B=S/IS$. Then $A$ is nonzero, reduced and Noetherian, $A\to B$ is flat and finite type with geometrically integral fibres, $B$ is not $A$-projective, and $B/JB$ is $A/J$-projective for every nonzero ideal $J\subseteq A$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, first proof paragraph: maximal bad ideal and radical reduction, including preservation under quotient base change; translation of geometric integrality into the ring condition expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-reduced-algebra-generic-completion-cover] to $A\to B$. Write $f\ne0$ for its element, $C=\varprojlim A/(f^n)$ and $D=B\otimes_A C$. It gives $B_f$ free over $A_f$, faithful flatness of $A\to A_f\times C$, Noetherianity and $fC$-adic completeness of $C$, finite type and flatness of $C\to D$, geometrically integral fibres, and projectivity of $D/fD$ over $C/fC$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, second proof paragraph: generic freeness on a domain localization, localization/completion cover, and projective reduction of the completed base change

proof.text: For each prime of $C$, take the identity field extension in the preceding geometric-integrality conclusion. Its fibre is a nonzero integral domain. Thus [lem-trf-complete-flat-integral-fibres-projective], with base $C$, ideal $fC$ and algebra $D$, applies and makes $D$ projective over $C$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, last proof paragraph: associated primes of integral fibres, properness over the complete base, and application of Tag 05DP (lemma-flat-pure-over-complete-projective)

proof.text: Put $E=A_f\times C$. The map $B\otimes_AE\to B_f\times D$, $b\otimes(a,c)\mapsto(b\otimes a,b\otimes c)$, has inverse defined on the two summands by $(b\otimes a,0)\mapsto b\otimes(a,0)$ and $(0,b\otimes c)\mapsto b\otimes(0,c)$. The tensor relations make these maps well defined and inverse [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. To lift a map from the free module $B_f$ along a surjection, choose preimages of the images of its basis vectors and extend linearly; hence $B_f$ is projective. Step 3 makes $D$ projective. Any $E$-module $M$ decomposes as $e_1M\oplus e_2M$ for $e_1=(1,0)$ and $e_2=(0,1)$, since $e_1+e_2=1$ and $e_1e_2=0$. For a surjection $q:M\to N$, an element $y=e_i y$ has a preimage $e_i x$ whenever $q(x)=y$, so $e_iM\to e_iN$ is surjective. Any map from $B_f\times D$ restricts to these components; their projective lifts combine to an $E$-linear lift [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus $B\otimes_AE$ is projective over $E$. The swap $e\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes e$, with inverse $b\otimes e\mapsto e\otimes b$, is $E$-linear by tensor balancing, so $E\otimes_AB$ is projective too. Apply [lem-trf-local-projective-faithfully-flat-descent] along the faithfully flat map of Step 2 to conclude that $B$ is projective over $A$, contradicting Step 1. Consequently the original $S$ is projective over $R$.
